\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Interpolation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Bobkov.Interpolation
\section{Overview}
Symmetric averages of profile-vector lengths admit a contraction inequality whenever the profile satisfies the scalar two-point bound. The auxiliary squared-length parameter records the remaining displacement variance.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric average length]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p022-b001}
For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb R$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, define $L(t,c)=\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+tb)^2+c+\|u+tv\|_2^2}+\sqrt{P(a-tb)^2+c+\|u-tv\|_2^2}\bigr)$. The symmetric average length is $L(t,c)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric interpolation deficit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairDeficit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength}
For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb R$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, define $L(t,c)=\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+tb)^2+c+\|u+tv\|_2^2}+\sqrt{P(a-tb)^2+c+\|u-tv\|_2^2}\bigr)$. The interpolation deficit is $\Delta(t,c)=L(t,c)-L(1,c+b^2(1-t^2))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonpositivity from bounded half-steps]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.nonpos_of_bddAbove_of_half_step}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $s$ be a subset of a set $X$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb R$. If the image $f(s)$ is
bounded above and, for every $x\in s$, there is a $y\in s$ such that $f(x)\le f(y)/2$,
then $f(x)\le0$ for every $x\in s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Subadditivity of the square root]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.sqrt_add_le_add_sqrt}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For nonnegative real numbers $x$ and $y$, one has $\sqrt{x+y}\leq \sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Evenness of symmetric average length]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_neg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength}
\difficulty{1}
For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, real numbers $a,b,t,c$, and vectors
$u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the symmetric average length satisfies $L(-t,c)=L(t,c)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetry under absolute displacement]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_abs}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_neg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, let $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb
R$, and let $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$. The symmetric average length at displacement $|t|$ and
parameter $c$ equals its value at displacement $t$ and parameter $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Probability along a symmetric segment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.probability_mem}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For real numbers $a,b,t$, if $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$ and $-1\le t\le1$, then $a+tb\in[0,1]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concavity in the additional squared length]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.concaveOn_pairLength_clock}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength}
\difficulty{5}
For any $m\ge 0$, profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, real numbers $a,b$, and vectors
$u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the function $c\mapsto L(1,c)$ is concave on $[0,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of the pair length]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.continuousOn_pairLength_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.probability_mem}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$, and let $a,b\in\mathbb R$
satisfy $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$. For any $m\ge 0$ and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the function
$t\mapsto L(t,0)$ is continuous on $[0,1]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Additional squared length bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_clock_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.sqrt_add_le_add_sqrt}
\difficulty{4}
For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, real numbers $a,b,t$, and vectors
$u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, let $L(t,c)$ be their symmetric average length. For every $c\ge0$,
$L(t,c)\le\sqrt c+L(t,0)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Adaptive midpoint bound for average length]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_adaptive_midpoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.probability_mem, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.carried_midpoint}
\difficulty{6}
Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative on
$[0,1]$, and suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$,
$P(a)\le\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)$. For real $a,b,t,c$
with $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, $t\in[0,1]$, and $c\ge0$, and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the
symmetric average length at $(t,c)$ is at most the average of its values at
$(1,c+((1-t)b)^2)$ and $(2t-1,c+((1-t)b)^2)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lower bound by the clock parameter]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.sqrt_clock_le_pairLength}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength}
\difficulty{4}
For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, real numbers $a,b,t,c$, and vectors
$u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, one has $\sqrt c\le L(t,c)$, where the real square root is zero for
negative arguments.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded interpolation deficits]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.bddAbove_pairDeficit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.continuousOn_pairLength_zero, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairDeficit, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_clock_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.sqrt_clock_le_pairLength}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$, and let $a,b\in\mathbb R$
satisfy $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$. For any $m\ge 0$ and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the interpolation
deficits $\Delta(t,c)$ are bounded above as $(t,c)$ ranges over $[0,1]\times[0,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One-step bound for the interpolation deficit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairDeficit_half_step}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.concaveOn_pairLength_clock, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairDeficit, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_abs, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_adaptive_midpoint}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $P(x)\ge0$ for
every $x\in[0,1]$, and suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$,
$P(a)\le\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)$. For real $a,b,t,c$
with $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, $t\in[0,1]$, and $c\ge0$, and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the
interpolation deficit at $(t,c)$ is at most half the deficit at
$\bigl(|2t-1|,c+((1-t)b)^2\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetric endpoint length comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_le_endpoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.bddAbove_pairDeficit, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.nonpos_of_bddAbove_of_half_step, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairDeficit, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairDeficit_half_step, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$ and nonnegative there, and
suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$,
$P(a)\le\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)$. For real $a,b,t,c$
with $a+b,a-b,t\in[0,1]$ and $c\ge0$, and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, one has
$L(t,c)\le L(1,c+b^2(1-t^2))$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetric pair contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_contraction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.pairLength_le_endpoint}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$ and nonnegative there, and
suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$,
$P(a)\le\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)$. For real $a,b,t$
with $a+b,a-b,t\in[0,1]$ and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the symmetric average lengths
satisfy $L(t,(tb)^2)\le L(1,b^2)$.
\end{lemma}
